What changed: The mgmt_methylation fixed effect in the locked v1.0 discovery formula was removed.
Reason: MGMT is absent from all eight of the Johnson supplementary covariate sheets used to build the clinical canonical table.
Affected results: All discovery estimates are fitted without MGMT adjustment; the effective formula is reported alongside the locked formula.

Item: 1p19q status derived as an IDH-subtype proxy
What changed: codeletion_1p19q was mapped from the recorded molecular subtype (Oligodendroglioma -> codel; Astrocytoma -> non_codel) rather than a molecular 1p19q call.
Reason: No molecular 1p19q call is available in any supplementary sheet.
Affected results: 1p19q enters the model as a two-level proxy covariate (43 non-codel / 28 codel patients).

Item: Tumour purity derived from single-nucleus malignant-cell fraction
What changed: estimate_purity was computed as rna_malignant_cell_number / rna_cell_number instead of a bulk ESTIMATE or ABSOLUTE purity.
Reason: No bulk purity estimate is available for the single-nucleus discovery set.
Affected results: Purity enters the discovery model as a continuous covariate (median 0.729).

Item: Cell-level QC applied on the full gene space
What changed: Cell QC (min_genes = 300) is evaluated on the full 36,601-gene expression matrix before the ~2,000 highly variable gene subset is taken.
Reason: Applying the same thresholds after HVG subsetting removed roughly four times more cells than intended and lost 33 of 75 samples.
Affected results: All discovery proportions derive from the recovered 75-sample design (221016 cells).

What changed: Each sample was uniformly subsampled to at most 3000 cells after QC (67 of 75 samples capped), reducing 437454 cells to 221016.
Reason: Bounded peak memory for the merge step on the available hardware.
Affected results: Rare cell types retain fewer cells, but the cap is applied uniformly and does not preferentially remove them.

What changed: Cell types were assigned from the mean marker score of each Leiden cluster (r = 0.8) rather than per-cell scoring.
Reason: Preserves cluster coherence and keeps cell-type assignment auditable at the cluster level.
Affected results: Only 5 of 10 primary types receive any cells; NK and Microglia are the only evaluable types.

Item: Optimizer fallback and zero-variance covariate dropping
What changed: The mixed model is fitted with lbfgs, retrying with bfgs then powell when lbfgs raises a singular-matrix error; covariates with zero variance in a given cohort are dropped from that cohort's effective formula.
Reason: Numerical optimisation failure and collinear terms, not a change in the hypothesis being tested.
Affected results: In GLASS, the constant purity proxy was dropped; discovery retained all terms. Optimizer identity is recorded per cell type in the model audit.

Item: Post-data power simulated with 800 simulation draws
What changed: Power was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation with NSIM = 800 and a patient-level design (seed 7331), at ICC 0.40/0.60/0.70.
Reason: A post-data power check gives an honest ceiling on what the recovered design could have detected.
Affected results: At ICC 0.60 the design reaches 61.9% power at f2 = 0.28 and 78.0% at f2 = 0.40; the headline label is UNDERPOWERED.

Item: GLASS deconvolution uses stock signatures with an added Plasma and Microglia row set, and no purity adjustment
What changed: GLASS fractions come from stock published signatures (quanTIseq/TIL10 for the primary fit) rather than the discovery custom signature; TIL10 was extended with canonical Plasma and Microglia marker rows; no purity term is fitted.
Reason: GLASS has no matched single-nucleus reference for a custom signature, and TIL10 models neither plasma cells nor brain-resident microglia; purity is not identifiable because the signature-mass proxy is near-degenerate.
Affected results: GLASS is reported as EXPLORATORY only. Verified in scripts/deconvolution_glass_pipeline.py (TIL10 extension block) and glass_pipeline_audit.json.

Item: Forest plot markers filled by BH q, no pooled diamond
What changed: Markers are filled when BH q < 0.05 and hollow otherwise, and no pooled meta-analytic estimate is drawn.
Reason: Pooling opposite-signed estimates across cohorts would be read as agreement between cohorts, which the data do not support; this deviates from pre-specification section 4.5(g), which allowed a diamond only when I2 heterogeneity was non-significant.
Affected results: Figure 3. Both cohorts' estimates are shown separately; no between-cohort heterogeneity statistic is reported because no pooled estimate is drawn.

Item: Signed direction consistency restricted to the discovery-evaluable types
What changed: The pre-specified >=7/10 direction-agreement test was retired; the GLASS direction comparison is descriptive and is limited to the intersection of cell types evaluable in discovery (NK, Microglia).
Reason: The plan-literal test cannot be evaluated when only two types are evaluable, and a 2-cell agreement count cannot support a claim of agreement.
Affected results: Both evaluable types flip sign relative to GLASS. No agreement count is reported anywhere in this package.

What changed: The immune compartment was re-clustered at resolutions 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 and evaluability re-assessed under the same >=10-sample rule.
Reason: Pre-declared to test whether the annotation step, rather than the data, limited which cell types could be resolved.
Affected results: The gate failed (1/2/2 of 10 evaluable); the primary annotation is unchanged and no mechanistic analysis followed.

What changed: Each deviation was verified against the named script or audit artefact. Where a claim could not be confirmed from project files it is marked [VERIFY].
